doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: The hustling route, gypsy groups and the Club De Lisa
summary: The group works a regular route ending at the Club De Lisa near dawn; neighborhood bars each had a small band.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Of course, we'd run in to gypsy groups out there hustling -- Spanish groups, French groups, everybody -- anybody would be out. Ask if they could come in and play a few numbers, you know. pass the heat Sure, come on. And we had a good jam session one time with a troop -- violins and that -- couldn't speak a word of English but they were beautiful. And we'd go our way and they'd go theirs. We'd try not to run in to each other, but we had a regular route

around Chicago, and say, about three or four o'clock in the morning, we'd probably wind up out around the Club De Lisa -- that was an institution in Chicago -- at 5th and State. A wonderful drummer had a band there for years, and Red Saunders, and he had Eckstein singing in there. Really top notch acts used to come through there. Run by the De Lisa brothers.

But as a kid, like I said, music was all around Chicago. In every neighborhood, they had a band --- every little bar had one. At least they would have a band in there. See, three pieces playing "Jumping at the Woodside" "Every Tub" -- trumpet, drum and piano. And they would play. They'd almost play the whole arrangement, you know?
